guide.summary: Shrines, castle ruins, art museums and family outings, with breakfast rooms, motsunabe dinners, hotel bars, a bakery and coffee shops checked against their own websites.
guide.tip: Plan museum days around staggered closures: the Fukuoka Art Museum, Fukuoka City Museum and the zoo close on Mondays, the Science Museum on Tuesdays and the Asian Art Museum on Wednesdays, each moving to the next weekday when that day is a public holiday.

toolkit.label: Closing days
toolkit.value: Mon, Tue or Wed by venue
toolkit.copy: The Fukuoka Art Museum, Fukuoka City Museum and Fukuoka City Zoo close on Mondays, the Fukuoka City Science Museum on Tuesdays and the Fukuoka Asian Art Museum on Wednesdays, each moving to the next weekday after a public holiday. The Hakata Machiya Folk Museum closes on the fourth Monday of the month.

toolkit.label: Tickets and booking
toolkit.copy: Le Champ d'Or at Hotel Okura Fukuoka is reservation-only and opens Friday dinners plus weekend and holiday lunches and dinners, while Yamazato closes on Tuesdays and Wednesdays unless they are holidays; both take bookings via TableCheck or the reservations desk on 092-262-1176 (10:00-18:00). Fukuoka Tower's observation deck costs 1,000 yen for adults.

toolkit.label: Walk-in and timing
toolkit.copy: Fukuoka Tower opens 9:30 to 22:00 with last entry at 21:30, which it says may come earlier when crowded. Canal City Hakata states it is open all year, with shops from 10:00 to 21:00 and restaurants from 11:00 to 23:00.

toolkit.label: Rules
toolkit.copy: Fukuoka Tower does not store luggage, offers coin lockers on 1F and asks you not to bring food or drink onto the observation deck. The Fukuoka Art Museum bans video, flash, tripods and selfie sticks, and Le Champ d'Or refuses entry in shorts or sandals.

guide.dek: Split your days by district and by closing day, keeping Dazaifu for a morning and Momochihama's museum and tower for an afternoon into evening.
intro: Fukuoka's public museums stagger their closing days, so a little planning goes a long way. The Fukuoka Art Museum, inside Ohori Park, opens from 9:30 to 17:30 and closes on Mondays. Its Indian chintz exhibition from the Karun Thakar Collection runs from 17 October to 20 December 2026, alongside a 150th-anniversary show on the printmaker Yoshida Hiroshi until the same date. The Fukuoka Asian Art Museum occupies the seventh and eighth floors of the Riverain Center Building, closes on Wednesdays and stays open until 20:00 on Fridays and Saturdays.

The Asian Art Museum's South Asia special edition runs until 11 January 2027. Out in Momochihama, the Fukuoka City Museum closes on Mondays and shows its special exhibition 1999 until 11 January 2027. Fukuoka Tower, also on a Momochihama address, opens from 9:30 to 22:00 with last entry at 21:30, which it warns may come earlier when crowded. An adult ticket for the observation deck is 1,000 yen, coin lockers are on 1F, and you are asked not to bring food or drink up to the deck.

For a slower start, Dazaifu Tenmangu opens its gates at 6:30 from the autumn equinox and closes them at 19:00 from September to November and at 18:30 from December to March. Back in Hakata, the Hakata Machiya Folk Museum opens from 10:00 to 18:00, closes on the fourth Monday of the month, and charges 200 yen, with elementary and junior high pupils free. The Fukuoka Castle Ruins in Jonai are free to enter except during events, and families can add the Fukuoka City Zoo and Botanical Garden, open 9:00 to 17:00 except Mondays.

At Hotel Okura Fukuoka, Camellia serves breakfast from 6:30 to 10:00 with no regular closing day, and the Pastry Boutique on 1F sells baguettes and kouign-amann daily. Yamazato closes on Tuesdays and Wednesdays unless they are holidays, and Le Champ d'Or is reservation-only and turns away shorts and sandals. For motsunabe, Ganso Motsunabe Rakutenchi's Sohonten in Imaizumi opens from 17:00 to midnight all year. Hotel Nikko Fukuoka's main bar, Yakan Hiko, has piano sets Monday to Saturday, with a 1,360 yen cover charge during performances.
summaryCards: Pair Ohori Park with the Fukuoka Art Museum inside it, remembering the museum closes on Mondays.
Take breakfast at Camellia in Hotel Okura Fukuoka from 6:30, then walk to the Fukuoka Asian Art Museum, which shares its Shimokawabatamachi address and closes on Wednesdays.
Le Champ d'Or takes reservations only and opens Friday dinners plus weekend and holiday meals, while Yamazato closes on Tuesdays and Wednesdays unless they are holidays.

limitations: Website review, not a visit or telephone confirmation. Advertised opening, booking and exhibition details do not guarantee availability, and Japanese-language pages were read through automated extraction. Several sites could not be read: REC COFFEE branch pages returned HTTP 429, Grand Hyatt Fukuoka returned 403, Trandor had a certificate error, and Hakata Hanamidori, DACOMECCA and Ishimura Manseido did not resolve; IPPUDO, ShinShin and Nokonoshima Island Park returned nothing readable. The Kyushu National Museum was dropped only because no page read showed its street address, and Kushida Shrine because no official site was found. Hours were not published on the pages read for Ohori Park, Fukuoka Castle Ruins, Uminonakamichi Seaside Park and Yanagibashi Rengo Market (whose only dated item is from January 2026), and Marine World's closing days were not readable; the site also flags a temporary suspension of its dolphin and sea lion shows. manucoffee and Hakata Machiya Folk Museum hours come from undated shop-list and access pages, and Hotel Okura's Pastry Boutique page gives two different closing times (20:00 and 18:00).
